model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net_debt = 0

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payments' C$15M (FY24 13, FY23 14; BNS.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:9100) and Q3-26 note 12 equity-settled share-based payment expense (9M-FY26 C$9M; BNS.TO_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:4165). The C$407M 'Share-based payments' in the compensation note (Annual_FY2025.txt:2237, the CSV StockBasedComp column) is overwhelmingly cash-settled share units already expensed inside non-interest expenses and settled in cash, so it is not added back; only the equity-settled charge dilutes and it is charged in the flows via sbc_pct_path.
inputs.fy0: TTM to 2026-07-31 (adjusted basis, pro forma for the divested Colombia/Costa Rica/Panama operations)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API, TSX BNS.TO, CAD)
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,219M common shares at 2026-07-31 (Q3-26 Report to Shareholders T1 'End of period'; BNS.TO_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:282) + 3M dilutive share-based payment options and others (note 21, Q3-26 diluted EPS table; :5489) = 1,222M fully diluted. One TSX share = one NYSE share. Held FLAT: the equity-settled SBC is charged in the flows and buybacks are a use of the FCFE being valued (C$1,011M repurchased in Q3-26 alone, 8.6M shares; C$2,138M YTD; NCIB running). buyback_cash is the Q3-26 quarter's financing-activity outflow.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY in CAD, not a WACC: the flow is post-interest, post-preferred FCFE to common. Canada 10y ~3.4% + beta ~1.15 x 5.75% ERP = ~10.0%; base 10.0%. Set 25bp above BMO/TD (9.75%) and 50bp above RY (9.5%), all valued the same weekend, because roughly a quarter of earnings come from Mexico, Peru, Chile and the Caribbean (EM credit, currency and political risk the domestic-only peers do not carry), BNS has historically run the lowest ROE of the Big Six, and its beta is the highest of the four. Bull 9.75%; bear 10.5% (only +50bp because the bear credit path already carries most of the downside -- charge risk once). Flows, discount rate and quote are all CAD, so no cross-currency step enters the per-share value.
inputs.lease_treatment: n/a -- bank; premises/lease cost is inside non-interest expenses, no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Preferred dividends + LRCN/AT1 distributions (TTM adjusted C$504M: FY25 506 less 9M-FY25 391, plus 9M-FY26 389) and NCI income (TTM adjusted C$144M less ~C$8M attributable to the divested operations = C$136M) are removed INSIDE the flow as a pre-tax equivalent (640 / (1 - 0.242) = ~C$844M), so the after-tax flow is net income to COMMON. Preferred shares and other equity instruments (C$9,939M at 2026-07-31) are therefore NOT also deducted in the bridge (BMO/USB precedent; doing both charges them twice).
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine (house precedent BMO.TO, TD, RY valued 2026-10-04/10, plus USB, TFC, HBAN, NTRS, STT, NAB.AX; SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book -- FCFE-at-CoE with retention = growth x regulatory capital is the equivalent flow form and keeps BNS comparable with the other Canadian banks in this folder). No prior valuation of this ticker. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = net interest income + non-interest income (adjusted); 'ebitda' = adjusted pre-tax income + equity-settled SBC - pre-tax-equivalent(pref/AT1 distributions + NCI); D&A 0; 'capex' = capital retention needed to keep CET1 at 13.1% as RWA grows with revenue = CET1/revenue 1.626 x g/(1+g); wc 0; net_debt 0 (deposits C$1,006B, wholesale funding and subordinated debentures are operating funding / regulatory capital, not acquisition debt). TTM BUILD (adjusted, C$M; Q4-FY25 = FY25 adjusted less 9M-FY25 adjusted): revenue 9,767 + 30,465 = 40,232; PCL 1,113 + 3,472 = 4,585 (11.4% of revenue, 0.60% of average loans -- above BNS's own through-cycle ~0.45-0.50%); adjusted NIE 5,308 + 15,984 = 21,292 (adjusted productivity 52.9%); pre-tax 3,346 + 11,009 = 14,355; tax 788 + 2,689 = 3,477 (24.2%); NI 2,558 + 8,320 = 10,878; NCI 40 + 104 = 144; pref/other 115 + 389 = 504; NI to common 2,403 + 7,827 = 10,230. ADJUSTED, NOT REPORTED: TTM reported NI (2,206 + 7,884 = 10,090) carries the Q1-26 C$434M (C$377M after-tax) cumulative-FX-translation loss released on closing the Davivienda transaction, the Q4-25 C$373M restructuring charge and C$74M legal provision, and acquired-intangible amortisation (~C$30M/yr pre-tax); these are removed. PRO FORMA: the Colombia/Costa Rica/Panama operations transferred to Davivienda on 2025-12-01 are still inside the TTM for Q4-FY25 (~C$400M revenue, ~C$30M NI, by the Q3-FY25 run-rate in T8B) and November 2025 (C$130M revenue, C$1M NI; T8B, BNS.TO_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:1092-1110), so FY0 revenue = 40,232 - 530 = 39,700 and pre-tax = 14,355 - 60 = 14,295; the 20.3% Davivienda stake is equity-accounted inside non-interest income from December 2025 and stays in the flow (no bridge item: its earnings are in the flow, so the asset is not added). ebitda = 14,295 + 15 - 844 = 13,466 = 33.9% of FY0 revenue; NOPAT = (13,466 - 15) x 0.758 = 10,196 = pro forma NI to common. CET1: 13.1% x RWA 492,866 = C$64.6B at 2026-07-31 (the run-rate target is ~13%, so the ~C$0.5B above 13.0% is immaterial and not bridged) = 1.626x pro forma revenue. last_fcf 6,645 = pro forma NI to common 10,196 less retention at 5.5% growth (64,565 x 0.055 = 3,551) -- an FCFE proxy, since bank OCF (C$-16.8B in Q3-26, +C$17.1B in Q2-26) is balance-sheet noise, not owner cash. KeyCorp (~14.9%, equity-accounted since Q1-FY25) and MapleMark (closed, immaterial) are already in the adjusted run-rate.
inputs.price_note: Regular-session TSX close (Thursday 2026-10-09), not an after-hours print; 52-week range 88.5-134.5.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (book value per common share FY2020 51.85 -> FY2025 62.22, CAD)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Reported EPS CAGRs diverge from BVPS by more than 30% (5yr EPS 1.4% vs BVPS 3.7%; 3yr EPS -10.9% vs BVPS 4.4%) because FY2025 reported EPS 5.67 carries the C$1.34B Davivienda impairment, the C$373M restructuring charge and the C$74M legal provision, and FY2022 (8.02) was a pre-impairment peak. Adjusted EPS FY2024 6.47 -> FY2025 7.09 (+10%) -> TTM 7.54 tells the forward story; BVPS 5yr 3.7% is also depressed by LatAm FX translation losses in OCI, so the forward base path (5.5% -> 3%) starts above it and is anchored to the ROE recovery (adjusted ROE 14.2% in Q3-26 vs 11.6% a year earlier), not to the historical CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: fcf_*_cagr fields carry REPORTED NET INCOME CAGRs (FY2022 10,174 / FY2020 6,853 -> FY2025 7,758): bank OCF/FCF swings with trading assets, deposits and securities and is not an owner cash flow. Adjusted NI FY2024 8,627 -> FY2025 9,510 (+10%); TTM adjusted 10,878. All CAD.

base.margin_rationale: Delivers the medium-term framework (adjusted ROE 14%+, positive operating leverage) without going beyond it: adjusted productivity 52.9% TTM improves ~0.5pp/yr to ~51.5% by year 3 (Q3-26 was already 52.5%), PCL moderates gradually from 11.4% of revenue (0.60% of loans) to ~10.5% (~0.52%) -- BNS's structural PCL stays above the domestic peers' because of International Banking; pref/AT1 + NCI ~2.0% of revenue. Margin 33.9% FY0 pro forma -> 36.0% by year 4, then flat. Implied year-3 NI to common ~C$12.7B on ~C$88B common equity = ROE ~14.4%, ROTCE ~17.5% -- at the target, not above it.
base.capex_rationale: Retention = CET1/revenue 1.626 x g/(1+g): keeps CET1 at 13.1% as RWA grows with revenue.

bull.margin_rationale: Productivity reaches ~50% (AI-led cost programme plus wealth/GBM fee leverage), PCL normalises to ~0.45% of loans (~9.5% of revenue) as Canadian mortgage renewals pass and the LatAm book shrinks to the better-quality Mexico/Peru/Chile core; ROE ~16%, ROTCE ~19-20%, in line with RY/NA rather than the historical BNS discount.

bear.margin_rationale: Failed CUSMA renegotiation tips Canada and Mexico into recession in year 2: PCL roughly doubles to ~1.1% of loans (~20% of revenue; FY2020 was 1.0% / 19.4%), revenue flat as loan growth stalls and NIM compresses with BoC cuts, Chilean and Caribbean mortgage impairments keep rising; margin recovers only to 32.5% (below today's 33.9%) because the productivity programme stalls and International Banking returns stay sub-par.

scenario_narratives.base: Scotiabank holds the ROE it has just reached: Canadian Banking keeps expanding margin (five straight quarters) with mid-single-digit loan growth, Global Wealth compounds AUM (C$474B, +16% YoY) and GBM stays strong but off the Q3-26 record pace, International Banking grows modestly from the slimmer Mexico/Peru/Chile/Caribbean core with the Davivienda 20.3% stake and KeyCorp ~14.9% stake contributing equity-accounted income. Productivity improves to ~51.5%, PCL moderates gradually as management guides, adjusted ROE settles around 14-14.5% and the capital above 13% CET1 is returned through the NCIB and a dividend growing with earnings.
scenario_narratives.bull: The North American corridor pivot works: KeyCorp delivers the ~C$350M/yr earnings contribution, MapleMark seeds a U.S. commercial franchise, Canadian rate cuts reignite mortgage and commercial lending, wealth and capital markets sustain double-digit fee growth, and the LatAm core re-rates as a growth asset rather than a risk. Productivity ~50%, PCL ~0.45%, ROE ~16%, and BNS closes its valuation discount to RY/NA.
scenario_narratives.bear: CUSMA renegotiation fails, broad U.S. tariffs return and both Canada and Mexico enter recession in 2027-28: Canadian unemployment passes 8%, pandemic-era GTA mortgages renew into losses, card losses among younger borrowers rise, Chilean and Caribbean impairments keep climbing, and PCL doubles to ~1.1% of loans. The Davivienda and KeyCorp stakes mark down. No solvency or funding case (CET1 13.1%, TLAC 28.6%, LCR 126%), but earnings power resets lower, the ROE target slips back below 12% and the market prices BNS at its historical discount to the Big Six again.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): the CUSMA renegotiation is a near-term macro binary that the bank's own outlook names as the path to a Canadian recession, PCL is already running above through-cycle and management has said moderation will be 'more gradual than previously anticipated', and BNS carries LatAm and Caribbean credit the domestic peers do not. Base 50%: Q3-26 (record quarter, adjusted ROE 14.2%, positive operating leverage for four quarters) shows the plan tracking. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs the KeyCorp/MapleMark corridor thesis, a benign credit cycle and continued fee-cycle strength to all hold at once, and the stock has already re-rated from a 1.3x to a 1.9x book multiple in a year. Same 25/50/25 as BMO.TO and RY; TD carries 30/50/20 for its U.S. plea.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what common shareholders can take out: adjusted net income to common less the earnings that must be retained to hold CET1 at ~13% as the balance sheet grows, discounted at the CAD cost of equity. Deposits and wholesale funding are operating funding, so there is no net-debt deduction; preferred/AT1 distributions and NCI are removed inside the flow. Flows, bridge, discount rate and quote are all CAD, so the per-share result compares directly with the TSX price. Scotiabank is charged a 25bp higher cost of equity than BMO/TD for its emerging-market earnings mix, and the base case holds the ROE it has just reached rather than extrapolating the Q3-26 record.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: PCL is 11.4% of revenue at 0.60% of loans; the bear's ~1.1% year takes ~C$4B pre-tax out of one year's earnings, and BNS's International Banking book (Mexico, Peru, Chile, Caribbean) is more cyclical than the domestic peers'.
Fee-cycle peak: GBM posted a record C$647M quarter (+37% YoY) and wealth AUM is up 16%; a market reversal hits year-1 growth and margin directly.

Adjusted vs reported: the model uses adjusted earnings; BNS has booked 'one-off' charges in four of the last five years (Bank of Xi'an, software impairment, Davivienda impairment and FX release, restructuring, legal). If such charges recur, adjusted overstates owner earnings.

Pro forma divestiture: the ~C$530M revenue / ~C$30M NI removed for the Davivienda-transferred operations uses the Q3-FY25 run-rate from T8B; the Davivienda stake's equity-accounted contribution is only eight months old.

Equity-accounted stakes: KeyCorp (~14.9%) and Davivienda (20.3%) earnings are inside the flow at the associates' reported results; a KeyCorp credit event or a Colombian peso devaluation flows straight through, and the capital charged against them is not fully recoverable in a bear case.
FX (earnings, not quote): about a quarter of earnings are in MXN, PEN, CLP and USD; a stronger CAD lowers reported CAD earnings and the FY0 base.
Terminal value carries most of the value; the 13x FCFE cap and 3% CAD nominal terminal growth drive it.
